subtitle: UPDATE Jul 27, 4:23pm BRT, 69 days from the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). NEW POLLING: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) (n=2,004, telephone, fieldwork Jul 24 to 26, 2pp margin, [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) filing BR-01489/2026) is the first national survey whose fieldwork sits entirely after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention. In the first round, Lula 42% and Flávio 33%, with Caiado 6%, Renan Santos 5% and Zema 3%. In the head-to-head runoff, Lula 47% x Flávio 43%. Against its own Jul 13 round, Lula gains 2pp and Flávio loses 1pp, both inside the margin, and the first-round gap widens from 6pp to 9pp. THE FINDING is not at the top: Caiado ties Lula statistically at 45% to 43%, the narrowest of the four runoff scenarios in the survey, which INVERTS the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24, published three days earlier, in which Lula beat Caiado 47% to 40%. Two top-tier institutes, fieldwork two days apart, opposite conclusions about which challenger is the most competitive, and the panel records the divergence without arbitrating. In the MARKET, the top stood still and the chasing pack moved: Lula stayed at 62.50%, Flávio rose 0.20pp to 23.85% and the gap stood at +38.65pp, while Caiado rose 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 1.95%, and went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50% in third place in the first round, in the same direction as the new polling. SERIES CORRECTION the panel owes to anyone who read it yesterday: the ceiling of Lula's price in the AFOS series is not 62.50%, it is 63.50%, marked in the early hours of Jul 26 after the capture, and the widest gap in the series is +39.80pp, from those same early hours. THE DAY'S EVENT was the third launch in three days: [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) formally nominated Romeu Zema in Brasília, still without a running mate, and his price fell 0.10pp to 0.55%, the third candidate in a row to be nominated and end the session lower. Total accumulated volume in the presidential market at USD 116.12M. Cross-check with live [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) Jul 27, 7:23pm UTC. CAPTURE CAVEAT: the double-reading lock BLOCKED both of today's rounds, the first over divergence in the second-place and third-place books and the second only in Caiado's third place, between 19.00% and 19.50%. The presidential book returned IDENTICAL numbers across all four readings over 17 minutes, which is why the winner prices enter as firm while the placement ones enter as a range.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 62.50% (flat, vol USD 7.68M accumulated), 69 days from the election. A second session with no variation. The gap over Flávio stood at +38.65pp. The ceiling of the AFOS series is 63.50%, marked in the early hours of Jul 26 after yesterday's panel capture, and the widest gap in the series is +39.80pp, from those same early hours. In the polling, [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27 has him at 42% in the first round, two points above the same institute's Jul 13 round, and 47% in the head-to-head runoff against Flávio's 43%.
fortes: He held the top of the series without giving anything back: 62.50% for a second day, with accumulated volume of USD 7.65M.
The day’s movement happened entirely between the second and third placed names, without touching his price, which points to an internal dispute in the opposing camp.
The Datafolha of Jul 24 keeps him ahead in all three runoff scenarios tested: 48% x 43% against Flávio, 47% x 40% against Caiado and 48% x 40% against Zema.
The launch of a third competitive candidate, Caiado for the PSD, produced no transfer of price against him: what gave way in the book was the chasing pack itself.
Personal approval of 49% against 48% disapproval in the most recent read, with the two ends swapping places compared with June.
fracos: The gap pulled back 0.80pp and came off the previous day’s peak, meaning yesterday’s record lasted one day.
There was no new poll to test the 62.50% level, and the distance between price and declared vote has had no fresh measurement since Jul 24.
The assessment of the ADMINISTRATION remains negative and is a different question from personal approval: 38% bad or terrible against 32% great or good.
The swap between approval and disapproval is 1pp in a survey with a 2pp margin, which is a statistical tie and not a reversal.
The week brings four national polls in five days, three with fieldwork after the PL convention, which means the current level goes into immediate testing.
candidates.analise: His second still day came alongside the first poll taken after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention, and the two together say more than either alone. On price, nothing: 62.50% for a second session, with the gap over Flávio at +38.65pp. In the polling, [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) (n=2,004, telephone, fieldwork Jul 24 to 26, 2pp margin, BR-01489/2026) measures him at 42% in the first round against Flávio's 33%, which widens the difference from 6pp to 9pp relative to the same institute's Jul 13 round. The two moves producing that widening, Lula up 2pp and Flávio down 1pp, sit inside the margin, so the widening is nominal and the correct reading is stability with a favourable tilt, not advance. In the head-to-head runoff he stands at 47% against 43%, four points, also inside the margin. The point that deserves attention is not the top, it is below: Caiado ties him statistically at 45% to 43%, the narrowest of the four runoff scenarios in the survey, when the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll three days earlier gave Lula 47% x Caiado 40%. On approval, Nexus brings 47% against 49% disapproval, versus 47% x 47% on Jul 13, while Datafolha on Jul 24 gave 49% x 48%. Two [statistical ties](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) with the ends in swapped order describe a narrow band around 48%, not a swing. Series correction, made here because the panel stated the opposite yesterday: 62.50% is not the ceiling of his series. The ceiling is 63.50%, marked in the early hours of Jul 26, after yesterday's capture. His accumulated volume at USD 7.68M, in a presidential market totalling USD 116.12M.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 23.85% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 7.68M accumulated), two days after the convention that formalized his candidacy. In the same session he fell 1.50pp in second place in the first round, to 76.50%, and rose 0.75pp in third place, to 7.75%. In the polling, [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27 has him at 33% in the first round, one point below the Jul 13 round, and 43% in the head-to-head runoff against Lula's 47%. Rejection of 50%, the highest in the survey.
fortes: Largest rise in the book on the day: up 0.80pp to 23.65%, comfortably recovering the 0.10pp fall recorded on the day of his own convention.
He consolidated second place in the first round at 78.00%, up 1.50pp, which reinforces the reading that he is the one who reaches the runoff if there is one.
His rise mirrors exactly Renan Santos’ fall, which indicates the market sees him picking up his competitor’s space within the same camp.
The Datafolha of Jul 24 records him at 32% in the first round, one point above June, and keeps the 43% of the head-to-head runoff.
The candidacy has been formalised since Jul 25, which closes the pre-candidacy phase and frees up the campaign calendar.
fracos: The rise came one day AFTER the event, which weakens any reading that the market took the convention as a gain.
The gain has an identifiable origin inside his own camp: Renan gave up 0.80pp, exactly what he rose, and Lula did not move. There was no advance on the front-runner.
Rejection remains the ceiling: 48% in the Datafolha of Jul 24, identical to June and the highest among all names tested.
The surrounding family names retreated on the same day: Jair fell 0.20pp to 1.05% and Michelle fell 0.40pp to 0.75%, dropping out of the 1% range.
He still has no running mate after Tereza Cristina’s refusal, and her price in the presidential book remains at 0.15%, with conventions running through Aug 5.
candidates.analise: His day was one of crossed signals, the opposite of yesterday's clean reading. In the winner contract he rose 0.20pp, to 23.85% (vol USD 7.68M). In the second-place contract for the first round he fell 1.50pp, to 76.50%. In the third-place one he rose 0.75pp, to 7.75%. Three books of the same name moving in three directions in the same session do not support a single narrative, and that is the honest record. In the polling, the first national survey with fieldwork entirely after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention brought no launch effect: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) measures him at 33%, one point BELOW the 34% of the same institute's Jul 13 round, with the difference inside the margin. In the head-to-head runoff he came in at 43% against Lula's 47%, the same level. And the structural number did not move: 50% rejection, the highest in the survey, above Lula's 48%. Away from the data, the story that dominated his day: Folha de S.Paulo reported that fund managers, economists and executives speaking on condition of anonymity are hoping he withdraws in favour of Caiado, citing among the reasons his closeness to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Senator Rogério Marinho, who coordinates the pre-campaign, replied publicly. It is reporting based on anonymous sources, not a finding by any authority, and it counts as context rather than as a procedural fact. The panel does not attribute the price move to it, because a new national poll came out and a third candidate was formally nominated in the same session.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 9.55% in the winner contract (flat, vol USD 8.56M accumulated), after two straight sessions of losses. He lost 2.50pp in third place in the first round, down to 62.00%, and gained 0.80pp in second place, up to 12.65%. In the new polling, [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27 measures him at 5% in the first round, above the 3% from [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) on Jul 24 and below the 9% from Real Time on Jul 21.
fortes: He keeps the third highest price in the presidential book and the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names, USD 8.53M, above Lula and Flávio.
He remains dominant in the first-round third place market, at 64.50%, far ahead of the runner-up there, Caiado at 15.50%.
He rose 0.10pp in the first-round second place market, to 11.85%, keeping the runoff hypothesis alive despite the fall in his main price.
His rejection in the Datafolha is 12%, a quarter of Flávio's, which preserves room to grow that the top two candidates do not have.
fracos: Second consecutive day of losses: he lost 1.40pp the day before and another 0.80pp today, going from 11.75% to 9.55% in two sessions.
He lost the 10% handle and gave up 1.50pp in the first-round third place market, meaning the loss was not confined to the winner contract.
Today’s fall has an exact counterpart in Flávio’s rise, which describes a market reallocating within the camp and picking the other name.
The distortion against polling is still the widest on the panel, 9.55% of price against 3% of declared vote, even though it narrowed through movement in the price.
Measured against the whole series, 9.55% is well below the peak of 17.90% on Jun 9, so the current level is a retreat from a level already lost.
candidates.analise: After two straight sessions of losses, his main price stopped: 9.55%, no variation. The movement was all in the sub-markets, and in opposite directions: he lost 2.50pp in third place in the first round, falling to 62.00%, and gained 0.80pp in second place, rising to 12.65%. Read together, this is the market taking the likely-third slot away from him and giving back a fraction of the runoff hypothesis, which is less contradictory than it sounds: losing third place to Caiado, who went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50% there, does not necessarily mean losing the chance of finishing second. In the polling, the new reading matters more than the price. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) measures him at 5% in the first round, which breaks the convergence at 3% that [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) on Jul 24, Gerp on Jul 22 and Indexa on Jul 21 had formed. The panel now has four recent readings at three different levels: 3% at three institutes, 5% at Nexus and 9% at Real Time on Jul 21. The dispersion between institutes, which looked settled on Friday, has opened up again. In the runoff tested against him, Lula wins 47% to 39%, the most comfortable margin of the four scenarios in the survey. The distortion the panel tracks, between 9.55% implied probability and declared vote, still exists and now has a less clear numerator, because the polling itself disagrees with itself. It remains a comparison between different quantities, probability of winning against vote intention. Series caveat: 9.55% is neither his high nor his low, with a peak of 17.90% on Jun 9 and a floor of 5.30% on Apr 26. Accumulated volume of USD 8.56M, the largest among the competitive names.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket): Caiado 1.95% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.15M), Jair 1.05% (flat, vol USD 5.25M), Zema 0.55% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 4.54M), Michelle 0.40% (down 0.35pp, vol USD 9.29M), Camilo Santana 0.40% (down 0.05pp), Haddad 0.25% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 6.38M), Alckmin 0.25%, Tarcísio 0.15% (vol USD 13.64M). In [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) of Jul 27, Caiado has 6% in the first round and TIES Lula statistically in the runoff, 45% to 43%, while Zema has 3% and loses 46% to 42%.
candidates.subtitle: Jul 27, 69 days out: the chasing pack had its best polling day of the cycle and its first day of convergence with price. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) put Caiado at 6% in the first round, the best of the pack, and two points from Lula in the runoff (45% to 43%), the tightest of the four scenarios tested in the survey. In the same session, the market moved in the same direction: Caiado rose 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 1.95%, and went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50% in third place in the first round. Going the other way, [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) formally nominated Romeu Zema for the presidency at a convention in Brasília, still without a running mate and with an Aug 5 deadline, and his price FELL 0.10pp, to 0.55%. It is the third launch in a row on the calendar in which the newly nominated candidate ends the session lower, after Flávio on Jul 25 and Caiado on Jul 26.

caiado.label: CAIADO ([PSD](/en/glossary#psd)), presidential Poly 1.95% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 5.15M) | third place in the first round between 19.00% and 19.50% (up 3.50pp to 4.00pp, range) | candidate formalized at the PSD national convention on Jul 26, with Kassab as running mate | BTG/Nexus Jul 27 first round 6% and runoff Lula 45% x Caiado 43%, statistical tie
caiado.fortes: He had the chasing pack's best day in polling and in price, and both in the same direction. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) puts him at 6% in the first round, the best of the pack and one point above its own Jul 13 round, and places him two points from Lula in the runoff, 45% to 43%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) inside the 2pp margin and the tightest of the four scenarios tested in the survey. In the market, he rose 0.20pp in the winner contract and, in third place in the first round, went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50%. It is the first time in two weeks that polling and price move together in his case. Add to that the Folha de S.Paulo story of Jul 27 reporting that part of the financial market prefers his ticket to Flávio's candidacy.
caiado.fracos: The contrast between institutes is too large to treat the new reading as settled: three days earlier, the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24 gave Lula 47% x Caiado 40%, seven points, and measured him at 4% in the first round against Nexus's 6%. Two top-tier measurements with fieldwork two days apart should not diverge that much, and there is still no third reading to break the tie. On price, 1.95% in the winner contract is still a low level in absolute terms, and a 0.20pp gain in a book that size is little money. It is worth remembering that his price fell on the very day of the convention that formalized him, on Jul 26.

haddad.label: HADDAD ([PT](/en/glossary#pt)), presidential Poly 0.25% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 6.38M) | not tested for president by BTG/Nexus of Jul 27 or by Datafolha of Jul 24 | focus on the São Paulo state race, ticket formalized on Jul 25 with Márcio França (PSB) as running mate
haddad.fortes: He remains the PT’s leading figure in the country’s largest electorate, with the São Paulo state ticket made official at a convention in Campinas on Jul 25, with Márcio França as running mate and Lula present, which closed months of negotiation.
haddad.fracos: A second straight session of losses: he gave up another 0.10pp and reached 0.25%, leaving the level he held before the state convention. No national poll tests him for president, including [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Monday and [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) of Jul 24, so his price is residual name recognition with no polling backing in the office being priced.

zema.label: ZEMA ([Novo](/en/glossary#novo)), presidential Poly 0.55% (down 0.10pp, vol USD 4.54M) | third place in the first round 4.65% | BTG/Nexus Jul 27 first round 3% and runoff Lula 46% x Zema 42% | FORMALLY NOMINATED by Novo on Jul 27, in Brasília, still WITHOUT a running mate, with an Aug 5 deadline
zema.fortes: He is no longer a pre-candidate: [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) formalized his presidential candidacy at a convention in Brasília on Monday (Poder360, Estado de Minas, Gazeta do Povo, Brasil 247, Jul 27). In [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg), he loses the runoff to Lula 46% to 42%, four points, the same difference as the scenario with Flávio, meaning he measures as competitive as the runner-up in a head-to-head matchup despite having 3% in the first round against Flávio's 33%.
zema.fracos: His price FELL 0.10pp on the very day of the convention that formalized him, to 0.55%, and it is the third launch in a row on the calendar to end that way, after Flávio on Jul 25 and Caiado on Jul 26. He is still WITHOUT a running mate, now with the Aug 5 deadline in sight and with two rivals in the same space already formalized. In the polling, his 3% in the first round is one point below the 4% of the same BTG/Nexus round of Jul 13, and he was the only member of the pack to fall in the comparison between the institute's two rounds.

candidates.analise: The chasing pack reversed yesterday's pattern: it had its best polling day of the cycle and, for the first time in two weeks, price followed. The centre of that is Ronaldo Caiado. [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) (n=2,004, fieldwork Jul 24 to 26, BR-01489/2026) puts him at 6% in the first round, the best of the pack, and two points from Lula in the runoff, 45% to 43%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) and the tightest of the four scenarios in the survey. In the same session the market raised his price in both books where he appears, 0.20pp in the winner contract and, in third place in the first round, from 15.50% into a range of 19.00% to 19.50%. Convergence between polling and price is more informative than price moving alone, and it is exactly what had been missing in his case. But the panel is obliged to show the other side just as clearly: three days earlier, the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24 gave Lula 47% x Caiado 40%, seven points, and measured him at 4% in the first round. Two top-tier houses, fieldwork two days apart, opposite readings on the same challenger, with no third measurement to break the tie. Recording the divergence is the panel's job; arbitrating it is not. Going the other way was Zema, formally nominated by [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) in Brasília, still without a running mate, with his price down 0.10pp on the very day, the third launch in a row to end that way. In the polling he measures 3%, one point below the same institute's previous round, and at the same time loses the runoff to Lula by only four points, exactly the same margin as the scenario with Flávio, the kind of contrast that comparing vote intention with a head-to-head matchup tends to produce. The rest of the pack retreated: Michelle fell 0.35pp to 0.40%, Haddad 0.10pp to 0.25% and Camilo Santana 0.05pp to 0.40%. The usual methodological caveat: these are prices between 0.25% and 1.95% in a book where the favourite is worth 62.50%, so movement in percentage points looks large in relative terms and is small in money.
fortes: Caiado had the chasing pack's best day on both sides of the cross-check: 6% in the first round and a statistical tie with Lula in the runoff (45x43) in BTG/Nexus, plus a 0.20pp gain in the winner contract and a 3.50pp to 4.00pp gain in third place in the first round.
Zema is no longer a pre-candidate: Novo formalized his candidacy at a convention in Brasília on Monday.
In BTG/Nexus, Zema loses the runoff to Lula 46% to 42%, the same four-point margin as the scenario with Flávio, despite having 3% in the first round.
Renan Santos, despite losing 2.50pp in third place, gained 0.80pp in second place in the first round and was measured at 5% by the new polling, above Datafolha's 3%.
fracos: Zema fell 0.10pp on the very day of the convention that formalized him, the third launch in a row on the calendar to end the session lower.
The new reading on Caiado flatly contradicts the Datafolha poll of three days earlier (45x43 against 47x40), and there is no third measurement to break the tie.
Zema is still without a running mate with the Aug 5 deadline in sight, and now with two rivals in the same space already formalized.
Michelle fell 0.35pp to 0.40%, her lowest level in the set, despite keeping the largest accumulated volume in the book among names other than Tarcísio.
None of them clears 6% in the first round of the new polling, and the highest price in the entire chasing pack is 1.95%, against 62.50% for the favourite.

cruzamento: Jul 27 was the Monday that tested Sunday. Start with what was missing and arrived: [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) (n=2,004, telephone, fieldwork Jul 24 to 26, 2pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-01489/2026, commissioned by Banco BTG Pactual) is the first national poll whose fieldwork sits entirely after the [PL](/en/glossary#pl) convention that formalized Flávio on Jul 25. And the convention, measured for the first time, produced no launch effect in Flávio's polling number: he came out one point lower. THE FINDING of the poll is below, not at the top. Ronaldo Caiado ties Lula statistically at 45% to 43%, the narrowest of the four runoff scenarios in the survey, ahead even of the matchup with Flávio (47x43). That INVERTS the [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) poll of Jul 24, published three days earlier, in which Lula beat Caiado 47% to 40%, seven points, the widest cushion in that survey, with Caiado measured at 4% in the first round against Nexus's 6%. Two top-tier houses, fieldwork two days apart, opposite conclusions about which challenger is the most competitive, and no third measurement to break the tie. AFOS records the divergence and does not arbitrate which is right: that is exactly the panel's job. Now the market, and here is the part that rarely happens. Lula stayed at 62.50% (vol USD 7.68M) for a second session with no variation, Flávio rose 0.20pp to 23.85% (vol USD 7.68M) and the gap stood at +38.65pp. The day's move belonged to Caiado, who rose 0.20pp in the winner contract, to 1.95% (vol USD 5.15M), and went from 15.50% to a range of 19.00% to 19.50% in third place in the first round. In other words, polling and price moved in the same direction on the same name on the same day, which had not happened in his case for two weeks. Convergence between the two sources is more informative than price moving alone, and it is worth recording with the same prominence a divergence would get. A SERIES CORRECTION the panel owes to anyone who read it yesterday, and which only surfaced when the full series was swept: 62.50% is NOT the ceiling of Lula's price. The ceiling is 63.50%, marked in the early hours of Jul 26, after the capture the panel published at 5:12pm UTC, and the widest gap in the series is +39.80pp, from those same early hours, not the +39.65pp the panel recorded yesterday. The panel stated the opposite and corrects it here, with the same prominence. The third axis is the calendar, and it closed a pattern. [Novo](/en/glossary#novo) formally nominated Romeu Zema for the presidency at a convention in Brasília on Monday, still without a running mate and with an Aug 5 deadline (Poder360, Estado de Minas, Gazeta do Povo, Brasil 247, Jul 27). His price FELL 0.10pp in the same session, to 0.55%. It is the THIRD launch in a row in which the newly nominated candidate ends the day lower, after Flávio on Jul 25 (down 0.10pp) and Caiado on Jul 26 (down 0.15pp). Three consecutive occurrences are no longer an isolated coincidence, but they still come with no cause asserted: these are small books, single-instant captures, and nothing guarantees the next convention repeats it. It stands as an observation to track until Aug 5, not as a rule. The fourth axis is reputational and came from reporting, not from data. Folha de S.Paulo reported on Monday that fund managers, economists and executives speaking on condition of anonymity are hoping Flávio withdraws in favour of the Caiado and Kassab ticket, citing among the reasons that he lied about his closeness to banker Daniel Vorcaro, of [Banco Master](/en/glossary#banco-master), from whom he asked for money. Senator Rogério Marinho, who coordinates the pre-campaign, replied to the piece publicly. It is reporting based on anonymous sources, not a court filing, and it is recorded as such. The coincidence that, on the same day, both the poll and the market moved Caiado up is recorded; the cause is not asserted, because three events in one session do not allow one to separate what moved what. The fifth axis is institutional and still has no price counterpart, for a fourth day. After Itamaraty denied visas, after the US denial of any intent to undermine the election, after Milei's attack on Moraes and the recall of the ambassador in Buenos Aires, on Monday the Argentine press reported that Milei will not apologise and China declared support for Brazil against external interference (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 27). Datafolha released a cut of its Jul 22 and 23 round in which 52% believe Trump's tariff push is meant to favour Flávio's candidacy, against 37% who disagree, running at 73% among Lula voters and 29% among his own. The market on the impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice stood at 3.40%, unchanged, in a book of USD 83 thousand that supports no narrative at all. A methodological caveat about today's capture, because hiding it would be worse: the double-reading lock BLOCKED BOTH of today's rounds. In the first, Flávio's third place (0.75pp) and Lula's second place (0.35pp) diverged. In the second, only Caiado's third place diverged, between 19.00% and 19.50%. The presidential book returned IDENTICAL numbers across all four readings, over 17 minutes, which is why the winner prices enter here as firm. The placement ones enter as a range, and Caiado's third place is published as an interval precisely because it was not confirmed. The sub-markets total USD 4.79M against USD 116.12M for the presidential one. The summary, with no value judgement: the polling confirmed the top and scrambled second place, the market agreed with it about Caiado and disagreed with it about Renan, and three candidates were formally nominated in three days, all of them ending the session lower. The week still brings [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) on Jul 28 at n=5,000, PoderData on Jul 30 and Vox Brasil on Jul 31 to say which of the two readings on Caiado holds up.
